gaps.term: outer two updates cost linear time
gaps.quote: The outer two cost linear time.
gaps.note: Unsupported and inconsistent with the page. D<-D-H is the same kind of address shear as the middle update H<-H+D (with the roles of the fields swapped and a sign changed), and the page says the shear needs the whole network and recursion to reach O(V u^tau). If the outer two were plain linear passes, so would the shear be. The page never says why these two are cheaper.

The page never says where mu<2^20 comes from. Neither the value of mu for the explicit network nor W_b, s_b is given, and the cited eta bound does not supply it. The reader cannot check this hypothesis, which the choice tau=1-2^{-50} depends on.
Auxiliary values and auxiliary wires are not explained or linked. The reader knows wires, banks and forward invocation, but not which wires are auxiliary.

gaps.quote: A forward, inverse, forward schedule of these invocations exchanges the two banks
gaps.note: An inverse invocation is never defined, and the cited claim is not tied to the interchange as the page has described it. The page reduces the interchange to three field updates of which only the middle one is a network shear, and this paragraph instead says a forward, inverse, forward schedule exchanges the two banks. Its role and how it matches those updates are not said.
